title: Unraveling the Microstructures of Additively Manufactured Multi-Component Alloys through Multi-Scale Characterization: Insights from SEM and Advanced STEM Techniques
content: Additive manufacturing (AM) has emerged as a transformative technology for producing complex, multi-element alloys with near-net-shape capabilities, offering significant advantages in design flexibility and material efficiency. However, the microstructures of AM-produced alloys are often highly complex, exhibiting significant variations across different regions due to rapid solidification and thermal gradients inherent to the process [1-3]. Understanding these microstructural heterogeneities is critical for optimizing mechanical properties and performance.
